gz12_access.topic: Access: the ban, the censor and the journalists killed

claims.text: In January 2024 Israel's Supreme Court upheld the ban on independent foreign press entry to Gaza on security grounds; the Foreign Press Association called the ban, then 95 days long, 'unprecedented'; outlets embedded with the army had commanders review material before publication.

Foreign reporters must sign an agreement to abide by Israel's military censor to get a press pass; the censor restricted subjects including security cabinet meetings and hostages; CNN requires all Israel-Palestine copy to be reviewed by its Jerusalem bureau, saying local nuances warrant scrutiny and that it does not share copy with the censor in advance; a November 2023 CNN standards directive said of Hamas statements 'We should be careful not to give it a platform'.

CPJ counted 192 journalists killed (at least 184 Palestinian) by 10 Aug 2025; the UN 242; IFJ at least 180; Costs of War found more journalists killed than in the US Civil War, both world wars, Korea, Vietnam, the Yugoslav wars and Afghanistan combined; Anas al-Sharif was killed in a targeted strike on 10 Aug 2025; a strike on Nasser Hospital on 25 Aug 2025 killed 20 including 5 journalists; Israel denies targeting journalists and accused some of militancy.

gz12_coverage.topic: Coverage in the US: newsroom rules, measured bias, ownership and opinion

claims.text: The Guardian reported, from six CNN staffers and over a dozen internal memos, that stories must be cleared by the Jerusalem bureau, that there were severe restrictions on quoting Hamas, and that Israeli government statements were taken at face value; a staffer called it 'journalistic malpractice'; CNN said its reporting 'has confronted Israel's response to the attacks'.

A New York Times internal memo first issued in November 2023 told journalists to restrict 'genocide' and 'ethnic cleansing', avoid 'occupied territory', use 'Palestine' only in rare cases and not use 'refugee camps' for areas historically settled by displaced Palestinians; it was reported by The Intercept on 15 April 2024.

The Intercept analysed more than 1,100 articles in the NYT, Washington Post and LA Times from the first six weeks: for every Israeli death Israelis were mentioned eight times, a rate 16 times higher per death than Palestinians; 'slaughter', 'massacre' and 'horrific' were reserved almost exclusively for Israelis killed by Palestinians; only two headlines mentioned Gazan children.

Skydance completed its merger with Paramount in August 2025, having promised 'viewpoint diversity' at CBS per FCC chair Brendan Carr; on 6 October 2025 Paramount bought The Free Press and named Bari Weiss, known for pro-Israel positions, editor-in-chief of CBS News, reporting to CEO David Ellison, son of Larry Ellison; the Free Press had published 'The Gaza Famine Myth'.

Gallup (Feb 2026): 41% of Americans sympathize more with Palestinians and 36% with Israelis, against 31% and 54% three years earlier; about two-thirds of Democrats and half of 18–34-year-olds sympathize more with Palestinians; about 7 in 10 Republicans with Israelis.
